_comment: What the crawler looks for. Edit this file to change the search; nothing
else needs to change. Phrases with spaces must stay in quotes so the search
engines treat them as phrases rather than loose words.
subjects are what gets searched for. recognize is the wider vocabulary used
to judge whether a result is on topic; a headline may say "reservoir solar"
when the search asked for "floating solar". Leave recognize out and the
Each topic produces one search per subject phrase. Topics marked per_state
are repeated once for every state below. Keep the lists short: both search
engines reject queries that get too long.
_relevance_comment: A result is kept when it scores 2 or more: a subject phrase in the
headline is worth 2, each angle word 1 up to 2, a state or county name 1.
Everything else is still stored and can be shown, just marked weak.
_limits_comment: GDELT asks for one request every five seconds and caps any single search
at 250 articles. max_age_days only affects how far back a run reaches;
articles already collected are never dropped because they aged out.
